name: TLA+
typeSystem: Untyped: TLA+ is built directly on ZF set theory plus temporal logic, so every value (numbers, tuples, functions, sets of states) is just a mathematical set; there is no compiler-checked type system, though the TLAPS proof system and TLC model checker can catch many classes of errors.
runtime: TLA+ specifications are not 'run' as programs; the TLC model checker exhaustively (or randomly) explores the reachable states of a specification to check invariants and temporal properties, while TLAPS mechanically checks hand-written proofs.

runtimes.name: TLC model checker (JVM)
runtimes.role: Explicit-state model checker that enumerates reachable states of a specification to find invariant violations or deadlocks.

runtimes.name: TLAPS proof manager
runtimes.role: Decomposes hand-written TLA+ proofs into obligations and dispatches them to trusted or automated backend provers; it is a proof orchestrator, not a TLA+ interpreter.

compilers.name: SANY
compilers.role: The standard TLA+ parser and semantic analyzer used by TLC and TLAPS.

concurrencyModel: TLA+ specifications directly describe concurrent and distributed systems as sets of possible behaviours (sequences of states related by a next-state action); there is no separate 'concurrency model' because interleaving is what the logic itself expresses.

codeExample.caption: A finite-state spec: a Boolean flag that repeatedly toggles
codeExample.source:
---- MODULE Toggle ----
VARIABLE flag

Init == flag = FALSE
Next == flag' = ~flag
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_flag

TypeInvariant == flag \in BOOLEAN
====
